paragraphs.heading: Methodology / Sparsification interventions
paragraphs.anchor: Q-Sparse selects the top-$k$ activation magnitudes~\citep{wang2024qsparse}.
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
Q-Sparse selects the top-$k$ activation magnitudes~\citep{wang2024qsparse}.
Spark Transformer motivates its statistical top-$k$ approximation by the
overhead of sorting-based selection~\citep{you2025spark}.
We take a simpler route: extend the FFN design of elementwise nonlinearities
to the query, key and value operands of self-attention, using a symmetric
threshold. A fixed cutoff needs neither ranking nor input-dependent moment
estimates. It leaves the retained activation count free to change as training
reshapes the distribution, instead of targeting a prescribed count.

paragraphs.heading: Methodology / Sparsification interventions
paragraphs.anchor: A sparsification intervention specifies where to set activations to zero
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
A sparsification intervention specifies where to set activations to zero
(nonlinearity sites $\mathcal{N}$), the nonlinearity and threshold, and where to encourage
small activations during training (pressure sites $\mathcal{P}$). The two site
sets need not coincide.

paragraphs.heading: Methodology / Sparsification interventions
paragraphs.anchor: We use ReLU and two thresholding nonlinearities:
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
We use ReLU and two thresholding nonlinearities:
$G_{+,\kappa}(x)=x\mathbf{1}\{x\geq\kappa\}$ and
$G_{\pm,\kappa}(x)=x\mathbf{1}\{|x|\geq\kappa\}$, with $\kappa\geq0$.
One-sided thresholding removes negative values and small positive values;
symmetric thresholding removes small magnitudes while preserving the signs
and values of survivors. At $\kappa=0$, their forward maps are ReLU and the
identity, respectively. Appendix~\ref{app:interventions} specifies boundary
and derivative conventions.

paragraphs.heading: Methodology / Sparsification interventions
paragraphs.anchor: The threshold is fixed within each training condition. Our hypothesis is
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
The threshold is fixed within each training condition. Our hypothesis is
that the learned distribution can adapt to this nonlinearity, with activation
pressure providing an additional way to shape it. We examine that adaptation
through the quality--sparsity comparisons and signed activation distributions.

paragraphs.heading: Methodology / Sparsification interventions
paragraphs.anchor: Pressure uses $\mathcal{L}_1$: we take the mean absolute activation in each
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
Pressure uses $\mathcal{L}_1$: we take the mean absolute activation in each
targeted site--layer tensor, after the nonlinearity where one is applied, then average these
means equally.
\emph{Naive L1} optimizes $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{task}}+\lambda\mathcal{L}_1$.
\emph{Orthogonal L1} (OL1) adapts gradient-conflict
projection~\citep{yu2020pcgrad,hsieh2024bloop} to this pressure objective.
It makes a task-only AdamW update, then adds a pressure
correction preconditioned by the task's second-moment estimates. When this
correction opposes the adaptive task direction, OL1 projects out its
conflicting component. A positive trust budget caps its norm relative to that task
direction. This limits the pressure correction without guaranteeing preserved task
loss; Appendix~\ref{app:pressure} defines the procedure.

paragraphs.heading: Sparsification interventions / Sparsity and architectural reach
paragraphs.anchor: \emph{Activation sparsity} is the fraction of exactly zero entries at a named site.
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
\emph{Activation sparsity} is the fraction of exactly zero entries at a named site.
To weight zeros by the work they affect, we define \emph{model-wide sparsity}
as $\Smodel=N_0/N_{\mathrm{model}}$, reported as $100\Smodel\%$. Here, $N_0$
counts scalar multiplications with at least one zero activation operand in
the declared transformer-block matrix products. $N_{\mathrm{model}}$ counts all valid multiplications
in those operations and the dense language-model head; the head receives no
zero credit. Counts are pooled before division. The percentage refers to this
declared multiplication workload, not all operations or elapsed time. We count
only causally valid pairs in a full, uncached sequence;
Appendix~\ref{app:accounting} gives the exact counters.

paragraphs.heading: Sparsification interventions / Sparsity and architectural reach
paragraphs.anchor: The \emph{model-wide sparsity ceiling},
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
The \emph{model-wide sparsity ceiling},
$\Smax=N_{\mathrm{reach}}(\mathcal{N})/N_{\mathrm{model}}$, counts the fraction
of that workload whose zero operand is guaranteed by setting the selected
sites to 100\% activation sparsity, crediting each affected multiplication once. It depends on the architecture,
site set, and sequence length, but not pressure or a checkpoint. The ceiling
characterizes selected-site reach rather than sparsity achievable at acceptable
quality: observed $\Smodel$ also includes natural zeros outside that reach.
Appendix~\ref{app:ceiling} defines the reach accounting.

paragraphs.heading: Experimental study
paragraphs.anchor: We pretrain randomly initialized Pythia-14M, 70M, and 410M
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
We pretrain randomly initialized Pythia-14M, 70M, and 410M
models~\citep{biderman2023pythia} on MiniPile~\citep{kaddour2023minipile}.
Detailed comparisons use 14M; the larger models cover selected recipes.
Quality is next-token validation cross-entropy, where lower is better.
We measure loss and $\Smodel$ in the same forward pass over all 338 complete
2,048-token blocks from the 500 MiniPile validation documents, excluding the
1,444-token tail. All training-result figures and tables use this evaluation.

paragraphs.heading: Experimental study
paragraphs.anchor: Within each size, matched contrasts share initialization, data order, and
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
Within each size, matched contrasts share initialization, data order, and
training budget. Adding pressure at fixed nonlinearities measures its additional
quality and sparsity effects; repeating the contrast across thresholds tests
how those effects depend on thresholding. Comparing A4 with A7 without
pressure examines broader nonlinearity placement. A4-OL1 versus A7-OL1 changes both
nonlinearity and pressure sites, so it compares complete recipes rather than isolating
nonlinearity placement at a fixed pressure objective.

paragraphs.heading: Experimental study
paragraphs.anchor: The cohort contains 30 conditions at 14M and 12 at each larger size.
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
The cohort contains 30 conditions at 14M and 12 at each larger size.
Each trains for 712 updates and 1.493 billion
input tokens; we evaluate the final checkpoint. Local pressure varies
$\lambda\in\{0.05,0.1,0.5,1\}$; A4/A7 vary
$\kappa\in\{0,0.01,0.05,0.1,0.5\}$. Multisite OL1 uses $\lambda=1$,
and all OL1 conditions use trust budget 1. Sweeping these settings tests
whether an added intervention has a consistent effect or depends on the
strength of the existing intervention. Appendix~\ref{app:training-protocol} gives the
optimizer, precision and learning-rate settings.

paragraphs.heading: Experimental study
paragraphs.anchor: For the evaluation-only reference, we apply uniform magnitude-clipping targets
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
For the evaluation-only reference, we apply uniform magnitude-clipping targets
$p=0,0.1,\ldots,0.9$ at $a,m,h,z$ without updating weights. Site--layer
thresholds are calibrated separately on ten training blocks. This is a
uniform TEAL-style control~\citep{liu2024teal}, not a reproduction of an
optimized allocation across sites. The main figures show A0 clipping;
Appendix~\ref{app:clipping-results} includes all 540 evaluations across the
54 trained checkpoints.

paragraphs.heading: Quality--sparsity trade-offs
paragraphs.anchor: Local pressure and broader nonlinearities offer different quality--sparsity trade-offs
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
Local pressure and broader nonlinearities offer different quality--sparsity trade-offs
(Figure~\ref{fig:quality-sparsity-overview}). With OL1 at $h$, the model can
improve validation loss while introducing modest model-wide sparsity:
at $\lambda=0.5$, A1-H-OL1 reaches $3.768\%$ sparsity at loss 5.1102,
compared with A0's loss of 5.2086. A0 post-hoc clipping reaches a similar
sparsity level, $3.832\%$ at target $p=0.3$, but with loss 5.3619. Thus,
similar aggregate sparsity can carry different quality costs depending on
the trained recipe and evaluation-time intervention.

paragraphs.heading: Quality--sparsity trade-offs
paragraphs.anchor: Broader interventions reach much greater sparsity. A7-OL1 at $\kappa=0.5$
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
Broader interventions reach much greater sparsity. A7-OL1 at $\kappa=0.5$
attains $27.483\%$ model-wide sparsity at loss 5.8294, accepting a quality
cost relative to A0. This comparison also changes computational reach:
the A0 clipping reference acts at $a,m,h,z$, whereas A7 additionally thresholds
the internal attention operands. At 14M, these site sets have analytic sparsity
ceilings of $12.833\%$ and $29.952\%$, respectively. This comparison changes
both the trained representation and the computation the selected sites can
affect. Paired comparisons separate the additions that produce the trade-off. Full endpoints
and clipping trajectories are given in Appendix~\ref{app:complete-results}.

paragraphs.heading: Quality--sparsity trade-offs
paragraphs.anchor: Broader interventions reach much greater sparsity. A7-OL1 at $\kappa=0.5$
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
Broader interventions reach much greater sparsity. A7-OL1 at $\kappa=0.5$
attains $27.483\%$ model-wide sparsity at loss 5.8294, accepting a quality
cost relative to A0. This comparison also changes computational reach:
the A0 clipping reference acts at $a,m,h,z$, whereas A7 additionally thresholds
the internal attention operands. At 14M, these site sets have analytic sparsity
ceilings of $12.833\%$ and $29.952\%$, respectively. This comparison changes
both the trained representation and the computation the selected sites can
affect. Paired comparisons separate the additions that produce the trade-off. Full endpoints
and clipping trajectories are given in Appendix~\ref{app:complete-results}.

paragraphs.heading: Quality--sparsity trade-offs / Paired intervention effects
paragraphs.anchor: Pressure's additional value depends on the threshold and target set
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
Pressure's additional value depends on the threshold and target set
(Figure~\ref{fig:paired-intervention-effects}). Replacing GELU with ReLU
alone increases model-wide sparsity by 2.714 percentage points (pp), but
raises loss by 0.0611. Adding local pressure improves loss relative to this
ReLU control. Changing naive L1 to OL1 lowers loss at three of the four
matched weights, but reverses that improvement at $\lambda=1$; the update
rule is not uniformly better across the sweep.

paragraphs.heading: Quality--sparsity trade-offs / Paired intervention effects
paragraphs.anchor: For A4, adding OL1 improves both loss and sparsity at $\kappa=0$ and 0.01.
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
For A4, adding OL1 improves both loss and sparsity at $\kappa=0$ and 0.01.
At larger thresholds it adds sparsity at increasing quality cost. At
$\kappa=0.5$, the increment is 2.498 pp for $+0.3783$ loss. The corresponding
A7 pressure addition yields 12.096 pp for $+0.1265$ loss, while at
$\kappa=0.1$ it yields 1.372 pp for a much smaller $+0.0008$ loss change.
Broader thresholding also contributes without pressure: A7 minus A4 at
$\kappa=0.5$ adds 5.171 pp for $+0.0432$ loss.

paragraphs.heading: Quality--sparsity trade-offs / Paired intervention effects
paragraphs.anchor: Pressure therefore needs to be evaluated at its actual threshold and sites.
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
Pressure therefore needs to be evaluated at its actual threshold and sites.
Its larger gain under A7 also involves more pressure targets and a different
objective normalization; it cannot be assigned to nonlinearity placement alone.
We next examine the distributions learned by these complete recipes.

paragraphs.heading: Paired intervention effects / Reshaping activation distributions
paragraphs.anchor: More FFN zeros need not mean more model-wide sparsity
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
More FFN zeros need not mean more model-wide sparsity
(Figure~\ref{fig:activation-reshaping}). At
$\kappa=0.5$, A4-OL1 places $99.31\%$ of pooled FFN elements exactly at
zero, compared with $93.64\%$ for A7-OL1. Their attention distributions
differ more sharply: A4-OL1 has a narrow nonzero peak and only $0.22\%$
exact zeros, whereas A7-OL1 has $95.60\%$ exact zeros and nonzero density
outside the symmetric threshold gap. The omitted zero masses are reported
in Table~\ref{tab:density-mass}; a narrow density peak is not itself a large
exact-zero probability.

paragraphs.heading: Paired intervention effects / Reshaping activation distributions
paragraphs.anchor: A4 does not directly threshold or pressure $q,k,v$, yet their distributions
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
A4 does not directly threshold or pressure $q,k,v$, yet their distributions
change substantially. This is a nonlocal response under the complete A4-OL1
intervention, consistent with spillover. The comparison with A0 does not
isolate pressure's contribution from the other training changes. A7 directly
intervenes at these attention sites, so its reshaping there has a different
interpretation.

paragraphs.heading: Paired intervention effects / Reshaping activation distributions
paragraphs.anchor: The operation counts show why this distinction matters model-wide. At the
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
The operation counts show why this distinction matters model-wide. At the
same threshold, $QK$ and $PV$ contribute 16.77 sparsity points under A7-OL1,
versus 0.06 under A4-OL1 (Appendix~\ref{app:operation-results}). Several
projection contributions are smaller under A7-OL1, but its attention
contribution more than offsets them. Greater model-wide sparsity can
therefore coexist with less pooled FFN sparsity. The scale comparison below
tests whether the A7-OL1 advantage over A4-OL1 persists in larger models.

paragraphs.heading: Paired intervention effects / Reshaping activation distributions
paragraphs.anchor: The operation counts show why this distinction matters model-wide. At the
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
The operation counts show why this distinction matters model-wide. At the
same threshold, $QK$ and $PV$ contribute 16.77 sparsity points under A7-OL1,
versus 0.06 under A4-OL1 (Appendix~\ref{app:operation-results}). Several

contribution more than offsets them. Greater model-wide sparsity can

paragraphs.heading: Reshaping activation distributions / Transfer across model sizes
paragraphs.anchor: The high-threshold A7-OL1 advantage persists at all three model sizes
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
The high-threshold A7-OL1 advantage persists at all three model sizes
(Figure~\ref{fig:scale-transfer}). At $\kappa=0.5$, A7-OL1 has both lower
loss and greater model-wide sparsity than A4-OL1 at 14M, 70M and 410M
(Table~\ref{tab:cross-scale-recipe-contrasts}). The zero-threshold ordering
does not transfer unchanged: A4-OL1 is better on both axes at 14M and 70M,
whereas A7-OL1 is better at 410M. Persistence concerns a specific recipe
relationship, not the entire threshold response.

paragraphs.heading: Reshaping activation distributions / Transfer across model sizes
paragraphs.anchor: Raw sparsity must also be read against the changing workload. The A7 sparsity
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
Raw sparsity must also be read against the changing workload. The A7 sparsity
ceiling rises from $29.95\%$ to $49.42\%$ and $87.25\%$ as the dense LM
head accounts for a smaller share of counted products. The bottom row uses
the same A7 denominator for every curve within a size:
$U_{\mathrm{arch}}=\Smodel/\Smax(\mathrm{A7})$. Because A7 reaches all
counted block operations, this ratio equals the block zero-product fraction
$\Sblock$. It removes the dense-head share while retaining the different
weights of operations within the blocks.

paragraphs.heading: Reshaping activation distributions / Transfer across model sizes
paragraphs.anchor: This is transfer of a complete-recipe comparison. The larger cohorts lack
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
This is transfer of a complete-recipe comparison. The larger cohorts lack
the no-pressure A4/A7 controls needed to isolate pressure's contribution.
They share a token budget rather than tokens per parameter, and 410M uses
a lower peak learning rate. Its A0 loss is also higher than 70M's under this
budget; the plot should not be read as a quality scaling law.

paragraphs.heading: Realizing sparsity with specialized inference kernels
paragraphs.anchor: Realizing activation sparsity requires kernels matched to the model's shapes,
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
Realizing activation sparsity requires kernels matched to the model's shapes,
nonlinearities and hardware. The released TwELL kernels~\citep{cetin2026sparser}
accelerated their supported workload, but the unchanged small-width primitive
failed numerical qualification for Pythia-14M. A shape- and sign-adapted
descendant, P0, qualifies on only four of our 30 checkpoints, with geometric
mean speedup $0.8910\times$ on that subset (Appendix~\ref{app:kernel-results}).
This motivates specialization for the architecture and intervention.

paragraphs.heading: Realizing sparsity with specialized inference kernels
paragraphs.anchor: To make this specialization practical within an architecture study, we use
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
To make this specialization practical within an architecture study, we use
a human-guided coding-agent loop to propose, test and refine implementations.
Execution and profiling feedback provide a basis for this
approach~\citep{ouyang2025kernelbench,luo2026agentic}.
We replay 42 eligible proposals from the Codex search against native PyTorch
scaled dot-product attention (SDPA) in CUDA graphs on one RTX5090.
The workload is BF16, batch-one, uncached 2,048-token inference with full
vocabulary logits. Qualification requires logits and loss to agree with the
native reference within specified tolerances on complete validation.

paragraphs.heading: Realizing sparsity with specialized inference kernels
paragraphs.anchor: The matched retrospective reaches $1.6024\times$ by iteration 11 and
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
The matched retrospective reaches $1.6024\times$ by iteration 11 and
$1.7830\times$ at iteration 42 on the fixed A7-OL1, $\kappa=0.5$ search
checkpoint (Figure~\ref{fig:kernel-autoresearch}, left): substantial gains
appear early, followed by a later improvement.
The selected implementation K050 qualifies on all 30 checkpoints in the
14M cohort, with geometric mean speedup $1.2340\times$. Speedup has a strong,
approximately linear association with model-wide sparsity
(right; OLS $R^2=0.8167$). This connects the logical metric to measured
execution, while checkpoint quality, topology and weights vary across the fit.

paragraphs.heading: Realizing sparsity with specialized inference kernels
paragraphs.anchor: Ablations distinguish fusion from the contribution of sparse paths.
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
Ablations distinguish fusion from the contribution of sparse paths.
Relative to the same fusion with sparse paths disabled, K050 is
$1.311\times$ as fast at the search checkpoint and $1.043\times$ as fast
geometrically across the cohort, helping 14 of 30 checkpoints.
Attention skipping is unprofitable in this workload:
disabling it improves every checkpoint, raising the mean to $1.2506\times$.
The attention kernel can skip a matrix-multiply instruction when either
complete operand fragment is zero; matching zeros in both $Q$ and $K$ are
unnecessary. Yet even substantial instruction skipping fails to repay its
overhead at 14M (Appendix~\ref{app:kernel-results}). The full-model gain thus
combines fusion with a conditional benefit from sparse paths: profitable
execution depends on both sparsity and the granularity at which work is skipped.

The matched retrospective reaches $1.6024\times$ by iteration 11 and
$1.7830\times$ at iteration 42 on the fixed A7-OL1, $\kappa=0.5$ search
checkpoint (Figure~\ref{fig:kernel-autoresearch}, left): substantial gains
appear early, followed by a later improvement.
The selected implementation K050 qualifies on all 30 checkpoints in the
14M cohort, with geometric mean speedup $1.2340\times$. Speedup has a strong,

paragraphs.heading: Discussion and conclusion
paragraphs.anchor: Pressure, thresholds and site placement need to be evaluated together.
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
Pressure, thresholds and site placement need to be evaluated together.
In the matched 14M comparisons, adding pressure ranges from improving both
loss and sparsity to exchanging quality for additional zeros. Extending the
intervention to internal attention can increase model-wide sparsity even
when FFN sparsity falls. The high-threshold seven-site recipe with pressure
improves both axes over the four-site recipe at all three sizes, but the
zero-threshold ordering changes. These results favor evaluating each
addition against its matched recipe, rather than choosing interventions
from activation sparsity alone.

paragraphs.heading: Discussion and conclusion
paragraphs.anchor: The interpretation is supported by a connected pattern across experiments.
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
The interpretation is supported by a connected pattern across experiments.
Matched comparisons identify how pressure's added effect changes with the
threshold; distribution measurements reveal which activations change; and
product counts explain their model-wide consequence. The high-threshold
A7-OL1 advantage recurs at all three sizes, while the zero-threshold reversals
identify where that relationship stops holding. Agreement across these
comparisons makes the result more informative than a favorable checkpoint
or an isolated sparsity percentage.

paragraphs.heading: Discussion and conclusion
paragraphs.anchor: Product accounting and kernel timing answer different questions. Counting
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
Product accounting and kernel timing answer different questions. Counting
zero-operand products shows where an intervention affects computation;
the sparsity ceiling explains how architecture changes that opportunity.
The kernel study confirms that some of it can reduce full-model latency,
but also shows that skipping attention work can cost more than executing it.
Fusion and sparse-path ablations are therefore necessary to attribute a
measured speedup.

paragraphs.heading: Discussion and conclusion
paragraphs.anchor: These conclusions concern MiniPile pretraining at a fixed token budget,
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
These conclusions concern MiniPile pretraining at a fixed token budget,
with a lower learning rate at 410M. Larger models test complete recipes;
the distribution diagnostics cover 14M and describe responses rather than
isolating a causal spillover mechanism. The kernel results use one RTX5090,
full-sequence inference, native SDPA and matched fusion controls. Transfer
to cached decoding, larger models and other hardware remains untested.

paragraphs.heading: Related Work / Sparsification interventions
paragraphs.anchor: Post-hoc thresholding removes activations that a trained model can tolerate
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
Post-hoc thresholding removes activations that a trained model can tolerate
losing. CATS thresholds small-magnitude activations
within FFNs, with both training-free and fine-tuning
settings~\citep{lee2024cats}. TEAL extends magnitude thresholding to attention
and FFN projections and uses block-wise greedy allocation to account for
their different sensitivities~\citep{liu2024teal}. These studies show that
site placement and sparsity allocation affect quality even without retraining.
Our uniform clipping control holds allocation fixed to provide a simple
reference for the trained interventions.

paragraphs.heading: Related Work / Sparsification interventions
paragraphs.anchor: Training-time interventions allow the representation to adapt to sparse
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
Training-time interventions allow the representation to adapt to sparse
computation. ReLU Strikes Back studies restoring sparse activations in
language models~\citep{mirzadeh2023relu}; ProSparse combines ReLU, progressive
$\ell_1$ pressure, and threshold shifting during continued
training~\citep{song2024prosparse}. ProSparse's schedule ablations show that
comparable FFN sparsity can carry different quality costs. Sparsing Law
studies how sparsity changes with training data, activation function and
model architecture~\citep{luo2025sparsing}, while \citet{cetin2026sparser} demonstrate highly
sparse FFNs induced by $\ell_1$ regularization during pretraining. Together,
these studies show that training can reshape the quality--sparsity trade-off.
We examine how pressure's additional effect changes with the threshold
and target sites, and weight the resulting zeros by the computation they affect.

paragraphs.heading: Related Work / Sparsification interventions
paragraphs.anchor: Extending sparsification beyond FFNs makes the choice of sites explicit.
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
Extending sparsification beyond FFNs makes the choice of sites explicit.
Q-Sparse applies top-$k$ selection to attention and FFN projection inputs,
reports overall sparsity and activated-parameter budgets, and ablates both
the sparsifying nonlinearity and the straight-through
estimator~\citep{wang2024qsparse}. Spark Transformer combines sparse FFNs
with sparse attention through token-position selection and examines the role
of its low-cost predictor~\citep{you2025spark}.
Projection-input sparsity and attention-position sparsity affect different
work. Our seven-site intervention also thresholds feature coordinates in the
query, key and value tensors used inside attention. We compare these broader
nonlinearities with projection-input nonlinearities, both with and without pressure at 14M.

paragraphs.heading: Sparsification interventions / Inference speedup
paragraphs.anchor: Converting activation sparsity into speedup requires an execution strategy
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
Converting activation sparsity into speedup requires an execution strategy
suited to the workload. TEAL accelerates batch-one autoregressive decoding,
where skipping weight accesses is valuable, and reports up to $1.8\times$
speedup at 50\% sparsity under its projection-based
accounting~\citep{liu2024teal}.
\citet{cetin2026sparser} address batched matrix multiplication: their TwELL
format packs sparse activations as a projection produces them and supports
fused FFN computation, reducing the overhead of materializing and consuming
the sparse representation. They evaluate throughput for full-sequence forward
passes, a different workload from token-by-token decoding. Spark likewise couples its
sparsity mechanism with an implementation that reports decoding
gains~\citep{you2025spark}. In each setting, skipped computation and memory
traffic must repay indexing, packing and launch overheads; operations that
remain dense limit the full-model gain.

paragraphs.heading: Sparsification interventions / Inference speedup
paragraphs.anchor: The execution strategy also depends on shape and sparsity structure.
paragraphs.original_paragraph:
The execution strategy also depends on shape and sparsity structure.
With larger batches, different token masks
can reduce the weight-loading savings available from sparsity, as Spark's
batching analysis illustrates~\citep{you2025spark}. Block Q-Sparse introduces
structure into the mask to accommodate batched
execution~\citep{wang2024qsparse}; TwELL instead makes packing and fusion
compatible with tiled computation~\citep{cetin2026sparser}.
Iterative kernel generation with execution and profiling feedback offers a
tool for exploring these
adaptations~\citep{ouyang2025kernelbench,luo2026agentic}.
We use this approach in a human-guided kernel case study, requiring numerical
agreement and full-model timings that include activation-dependent selection
and conversion costs.

paragraphs.heading: Introduction
paragraphs.anchor: Activation sparsity can improve language-model inference efficiency when specialized kernels skip computation and memory access associated w
paragraphs.original_paragraph: Activation sparsity can improve language-model inference efficiency when specialized kernels skip computation and memory access associated with zero activations. Recent work has shown that sparsity can be exposed in pretrained models through post-hoc thresholding or induced during training, in both cases with measured inference speedups~\citep{liu2024teal,cetin2026sparser}. These results raise a practical design question: how should a researcher place and combine sparsification interventions to obtain more useful sparsity at an acceptable quality cost? Answering this question matters when choosing which components of a recipe to retain, where to invest additional training, and which operations justify sparse-kernel development.

paragraphs.heading: Introduction
paragraphs.anchor: Existing approaches induce activation sparsity in different ways. TEAL applies post-hoc thresholding to pretrained models, ProSparse uses L1
paragraphs.original_paragraph: Existing approaches induce activation sparsity in different ways. TEAL applies post-hoc thresholding to pretrained models, ProSparse uses L1 regularization on FFN activations during training, and Q-Sparse applies top-k sparsification to both FFN and attention activations~\citep{liu2024teal,song2024prosparse,wang2024qsparse}. While each approach is effective in its own setting, it remains unclear how they compare under a common setup and how their effects interact when combined. An intervention that works well in isolation may add little on top of another or incur a different quality cost when applied at additional sites, making sparsity alone insufficient to identify which choices drive the improvement.

paragraphs.heading: Introduction
paragraphs.anchor: In this work, we study three sparsification interventions: (i) \emph{pressure}, an optimization regularizer that forces selected activations
paragraphs.original_paragraph: In this work, we study three sparsification interventions: (i) \emph{pressure}, an optimization regularizer that forces selected activations toward zero; (ii) \emph{thresholding}, a nonlinear activation function that maps small activations exactly to zero; and (iii) \emph{placement}, which determines where these interventions are applied. Under matched pretraining conditions, this paired design isolates the individual and interaction effects of each intervention and connects them to the amount of model-wide computation exposed to sparsification. Rather than report sparsity locally at individual activation sites, we define model-wide activation sparsity, $\Smodel$, as the fraction of forward matrix-multiplication products with a zero activation operand. We additionally derive an architecture-dependent sparsity ceiling, $\Smax$, corresponding to the maximum sparsity that can be achieved through the intervention set. Together, $\Smodel$ and $\Smax$ quantify the achieved and maximum fraction of model-wide matrix-multiplication work exposed to sparsification.

paragraphs.heading: Introduction
paragraphs.anchor: We pretrain Pythia-family models from scratch at multiple scales to study sparsification under controlled conditions~\citep{biderman2023pyth
paragraphs.original_paragraph: We pretrain Pythia-family models from scratch at multiple scales to study sparsification under controlled conditions~\citep{biderman2023pythia}. At 14M, we evaluate 30 training conditions across eight recipes, yielding 29 paired comparisons of pressure, thresholding, and placement. Broader thresholding produces substantially more model-wide sparsity than local FFN pressure, while combining thresholding with optimization pressure yields the highest sparsity. At the largest tested threshold, seven-site thresholding reaches $15.39\%$ model-wide sparsity; adding orthogonal pressure raises it to $27.48\%$ against a $29.95\%$ architecture-dependent ceiling. We scale selected combinations to 70M and 410M, where seven-site thresholding with pressure reaches $40.60\%$ and $80.62\%$ sparsity against ceilings of $49.42\%$ and $87.25\%$. Across all three sizes, trained recipes outperform uniform post-hoc thresholding in the aggressive-clipping region of the quality--sparsity frontier. Activation-distribution analyses further show that broader placement increases model-wide sparsity despite producing fewer FFN zeros because it also creates exact zeros in attention operands.

paragraphs.original_paragraph: Finally, we test whether specialized kernels can translate these sparsity gains into faster inference using GPT-6-Astra. Across 42 eligible development iterations, the selected implementation achieves a $1.78\times$ full-model speedup over native PyTorch/SDPA on an RTX5090 for Pythia-14M at $27.48\%$ model-wide sparsity, near its $29.95\%$ ceiling. Across all 30 14M interventions, speedup is strongly and approximately linearly associated with $\Smodel$ ($R^2=0.817$), showing that model-wide sparsity predicts realized speedup in this workload. Ablations show that both fusion and sparse execution contribute to the gains, while disabling attention skipping improves every checkpoint. The attention kernel can skip multiplication when either operand fragment is entirely zero, but detection and control overhead exceed the saved computation at this model size. Realizing speedups from sparsity therefore requires matching sparse-execution granularity and overhead to the available zero structure.

paragraphs.original_paragraph: Activation sparsity can accelerate language-model inference when specialized kernels skip computation associated with zero activations. Existing methods obtain sparsity through different combinations of training-time pressure, thresholding, and placement, but their relative and combined effects have not been isolated under a common setup. As a result, it remains unclear which interventions drive the gains, when they are complementary or redundant, and how much model-wide computation they actually expose to sparsification. We study these interventions under matched pretraining conditions across Pythia models. To measure their computational effect, we define model-wide activation sparsity $\Smodel$ as the fraction of forward matrix-multiplication products with a zero activation operand, together with an architecture-dependent sparsity ceiling $\Smax$. We find that broader thresholding produces more model-wide sparsity than local FFN pressure, while combining thresholding with pressure yields the highest sparsity. The combined interventions reaches $27.48\%$, $40.60\%$, and $80.62\%$ $\Smodel$ at 14M, 70M, and 410M parameters, corresponding to $0.918$, $0.822$, and $0.924$ of their respective sparsity ceilings. Trained recipes also dominates uniform post-hoc thresholding in the quality--sparsity frontier accross all model sizes. Finally, specialized kernels achieve a $1.78\times$ full-model speedup on an RTX5090 at 14M, and speedup across 30 model checkpoints is strongly associated with $\Smodel$ ($R^2=0.817$). These results show that activation sparsification is governed by the interaction between how zeros are induced, where they are placed, and how much of that zero structure can be exploited by sparse execution.
